title: Potential, Potential Difference and Potential Energy — 40 MCQs
description: Covers electric potential at a point, electron volt as a unit of energy, potential due to a point charge, variation of potential with distance and relation to field strength, equipotential lines and surfaces, and electric field between parallel plates in terms of potential difference.

questions.q: Electric potential at a point is defined as the work done per unit positive charge in bringing a small test charge from
options: the centre of a charge distribution
questions.explanation: By definition V = W∞→r / q₀ where the test charge is brought from infinity to the point.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric potential is
questions.explanation: One volt is one joule per coulomb.

questions.q: One electron volt (eV) is equal to
questions.explanation: 1 eV is the energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 1 V: e × 1 V = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

questions.q: The electric potential due to a point charge Q at distance r in free space is
questions.explanation: V = k Q / r where k = 1/(4πε₀).

questions.q: Electric field strength is related to potential by
questions.explanation: E is the negative gradient of potential: E = −dV/dx.

questions.q: Equipotential surfaces are surfaces on which
questions.explanation: By definition an equipotential surface is the locus of points having the same electric potential.

questions.q: The work done in moving a charge on an equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: Since ΔV = 0 on an equipotential surface, W = q ΔV = 0.

questions.q: For parallel plates separated by distance d and potential difference ΔV the uniform field is
questions.explanation: In a uniform field E = ΔV / d.

questions.q: Potential is a
questions.explanation: Electric potential is a scalar; only its gradient (the field) is a vector.

questions.q: The potential at infinity is conventionally taken as
questions.explanation: By convention the potential at infinity is chosen to be zero so that V at any finite point is finite.

questions.q: The potential at a distance of 30 cm from a point charge of 3 μC in air is
If the potential difference between two points is 10 V, the work done in moving a charge of 2 μC between them is
An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V. Its kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: KE = e ΔV = 100 eV (numerically equal to the potential difference in volts).

questions.q: The potential due to a point charge varies with distance r as
questions.explanation: V ∝ 1/r for a point charge; a graph of V versus r is a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.q: Two parallel plates are 4 cm apart and the potential difference between them is 200 V. The electric field between the plates is
The electric field at a point is 200 N C⁻¹ and points in the positive x-direction. The potential difference between x = 0 and x = 5 cm is
questions.explanation: ΔV = −E Δx = −200 × 0.05 = −10 V (potential decreases in the direction of the field).

questions.q: Equipotential surfaces around an isolated point charge are
questions.explanation: V = kQ/r is constant on spheres of constant r centred on the point charge.

questions.q: The potential energy of a system of two point charges q₁ and q₂ separated by distance r is
questions.explanation: U = k q₁ q₂ / r (taking U = 0 at infinity).

questions.q: A charge of +2 μC is moved through a potential difference of −50 V. The change in its potential energy is
The potential at a point 10 cm from a charge of 1 μC is 9 × 10⁴ V. The potential at 20 cm from the same charge is
questions.explanation: V ∝ 1/r; doubling the distance halves the potential: 9 × 10⁴ / 2 = 4.5 × 10⁴ V.

questions.q: If the electric field is zero in a region, the potential in that region must be
questions.explanation: E = −dV/dx = 0 implies V is constant (but not necessarily zero).

questions.q: The work done in moving a +3 μC charge from a point at potential 100 V to a point at potential 50 V is
Two points are on the same equipotential surface. The potential difference between them is
questions.explanation: By definition all points on an equipotential surface have the same potential, so ΔV = 0.

questions.q: The potential due to a positive point charge is
options: positive near the charge and negative far away
questions.explanation: V = kQ/r with Q > 0 is positive at all finite distances (taking V∞ = 0).

questions.q: An electron-volt is a unit of
questions.explanation: Although derived from potential, the electron-volt is a unit of energy.

questions.q: The potential at a distance of 50 cm from a point charge of 5 μC is 9 × 10⁴ V. The electric field at the same point is
questions.explanation: E = V / r = 9 × 10⁴ / 0.5 = 1.8 × 10⁵ N C⁻¹ (since E = kQ/r² = V/r).

questions.q: Three charges +q, +q and −q are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side a. The potential at the centroid is
questions.explanation: Distance from each vertex to centroid is a/√3. V = kq/(a/√3) + kq/(a/√3) + k(−q)/(a/√3) = kq √3 / a.

questions.q: A uniform electric field of 500 N C⁻¹ exists between two parallel plates. The potential difference between points 2 cm apart along the field is
The potential energy of an electron at a point is −4.8 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. The potential at that point is
Two parallel plates are maintained at potentials +100 V and −100 V. If the separation is 5 cm the electric field between them is
The potential at a point due to a system of charges is 20 V and the electric field is 10 N C⁻¹. Moving 2 cm in the direction of the field changes the potential by approximately
A charge +Q is placed at the centre of a spherical shell of radius R carrying charge −Q. The potential at a point outside the shell is
questions.explanation: Outside, the total enclosed charge is zero, so V = 0 (taking V∞ = 0).

questions.q: The work required to assemble three charges +q, +q and +q at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side a is
questions.explanation: U = 3 × k q² / a (three pairs each contributing k q² / a).

questions.q: An electron moves from a point at potential −50 V to a point at potential +50 V. The change in its kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: ΔU = q ΔV = (−e)(+100) = −100 eV; by energy conservation ΔK = −ΔU = +100 eV.

questions.q: The potential difference between two points 10 cm apart in a uniform field of 200 N C⁻¹ is 15 V. The angle between the field and the line joining the points is approximately
questions.explanation: ΔV = E d cosθ ⇒ 15 = 200 × 0.1 × cosθ ⇒ cosθ = 0.75 ⇒ θ ≈ 41°.

questions.q: A point charge +2 μC is at the origin. The potential difference between points at r = 1 m and r = 2 m is
Equipotential surfaces are always
options: parallel to the electric field lines
perpendicular to the electric field lines
questions.explanation: The electric field is the negative gradient of potential, so field lines are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces.

questions.q: The potential energy of a charge +q placed at a distance r from a fixed charge +Q is U. If the distance is doubled the new potential energy is
questions.explanation: U = k Q q / r; doubling r halves U.

questions.q: In a uniform electric field of 100 N C⁻¹ the potential difference between two points 20 cm apart measured perpendicular to the field is
questions.explanation: Displacement is perpendicular to E so ΔV = −E · Δr = 0; the points lie on the same equipotential.

questions.q: A proton is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 500 V. Its final kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: KE = q ΔV = e × 500 V = 500 eV.
